literature.headline_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期呼吸道合胞病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 荟萃分析发现,RSV感染儿童的支气管肺泡灌洗液中中性粒细胞百分比增加,巨噬细胞百分比减少。森林图显示中性粒细胞和巨噬细胞百分比的合并标准化均数差和95%置信区间分别为2.12(1.74至2.50)和−3.14(−4.16至−2.12)。综述结论指出,RSV感染儿童的气道中以中性粒细胞为主。 [10.1111/apa.70757]
在RSV感染儿童中,毛细支气管炎、咳嗽、鼻塞、呼吸急促、胸壁凹陷、啰音、吸氧、吸入治疗、糖皮质激素使用和住院更为常见(所有p < 0.05). [10.1007/s00431-026-07393-5]
总体调整后的VE在第一个、第二个和第三个RSV季节后分别对RSV相关急性呼吸道疾病住院/急诊就诊为81%(71-87)、64%(48-75)和60%(15-81)。 [10.1007/s40121-026-01438-w]
BXM在体外显著抑制了RSV复制并降低了IL-6的表达,在小鼠中则减少了肺部病毒滴度、RSV-F表达、IL-6表达、IKKβ/NF-κB激活以及RSV诱导的肺损伤。 [10.1128/spectrum.03825-25]

共鉴定出6,919例呼吸道病毒阳性样本。SARS-CoV-2仍然是最常检测到的病原体,其次是RV/EV、流感A/B(FLU A/B)、腺病毒、呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)、副流感病毒、博卡病毒和人偏肺病毒。在冬季观察到FLU A/B和RSV的明显季节性高峰,而RV/EV全年持续传播。对224例RV/EV阳性样本的分子特征分析显示存在显著的遗传多样性。儿童患者占了大多数的测序病例。 [10.1016/j.ijid.2026.109132]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: The meta-analysis found that children with RSV had increased percentages of neutrophils and decreased macrophages in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. [10.1111/apa.70757]

Bronchiolitis, cough, nasal congestion, tachypnea, chest retractions, rhonchi, oxygen supplementation, inhaled therapies, corticosteroid use, and hospitalization were more common among children with RSV infection (all p < 0.05). [10.1007/s00431-026-07393-5]
Overall adjusted VE against RSV-related ARI hospitalization/ED visits was 81% (71-87), 64% (48-75), and 60% (15-81), respectively. [10.1007/s40121-026-01438-w]
Hospitalization rates increased from 15 per 100,000 in 2024. [10.1371/journal.pone.0357303]

BXM significantly suppressed RSV replication and decreased IL-6 expression in vitro and reduced lung viral titers, RSV-F expression, IL-6 expression, IKKβ/NF-κB activation, and RSV-induced lung injury in mice. [10.1128/spectrum.03825-25]

The CDC published an update on respiratory virus activity levels, including information about respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). [news-b79db5af759c2b6d]. The article discusses the dangers of RSV infection in young children, highlighting its potential to cause severe complications such as bronchiolitis and pneumonia, and mentions prevention methods like maternal vaccination and infant immunisation with nirsevimab.

papers.title: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis Suggested That Neutrophils Predominated the Airways of Children With the Respiratory Syncytial Virus.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Aim The respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a predominant aetiology of early‐life respiratory infections. This systematic review and meta‐analysis compared the cell types involved in airways inflammation in children with and without RSV, noting that immune responses can influence long‐term complications and may involve different inflammatory cells. Method We searched for relevant studies published in English on PubMed, Embase, Google Scholar and Web of Science until 31 August 2025. Bias assessment was performed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist. Heatmaps were generated and forest plots were created, with I 2 values over 40% indicating heterogeneity. Results The search identified 126 studies and a quantitative meta‐analysis was conducted on six studies that comprised 202 with RSV and 97 unaffected controls. Compared to the controls, children with RSV showed increased percentages of neutrophils and decreased macrophages in their bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Forest plots revealed that the pooled standard mean differences and 95% confidence intervals for neutrophil and macrophage percentages were 2.12 (1.74 to 2.50) and −3.14 (−4.16 to −2.12), respectively. Conclusion Overall, this systematic review and meta‐analysis suggested that neutrophils predominated in the airways of children with RSV. This highlights the value of investigating these in future studies.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review aimed to investigate the predominant cell types in airways inflammation among children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection, focusing on the role of immune responses in long-term complications.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review included a systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Google Scholar, and Web of Science for studies published in English up to 31 August 2025. Bias assessment was conducted using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist. The meta-analysis was performed on six studies involving 202 RSV-infected children and 97 unaffected controls.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The meta-analysis found that children with RSV had increased percentages of neutrophils and decreased macrophages in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Forest plots showed pooled standard mean differences and 95% confidence intervals for neutrophil and macrophage percentages as 2.12 (1.74 to 2.50) and −3.14 (−4.16 to −2.12), respectively. The review concluded that neutrophils predominated in the airways of children with RSV.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review noted that I2 values over 40% indicated heterogeneity among the studies. However, the supplied evidence does not report specific controversies or unresolved mechanisms related to the findings.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings highlight the importance of investigating the role of neutrophils in RSV-induced airway inflammation for future research and clinical practice. The review suggests that further studies are needed to explore the implications of these immune responses on long-term complications.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigated the predominant cell types in airways inflammation among children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection. The review focused on the role of immune responses in long-term complications and compared cell types in RSV-infected children with unaffected controls. A meta-analysis of six studies involving 202 RSV-infected children and 97 controls revealed increased neutrophil percentages and decreased macrophage percentages in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Forest plots showed pooled standard mean differences and 95% confidence intervals for neutrophil and macrophage percentages as 2.12 (1.74 to 2.50) and −3.14 (−4.16 to −2.12), respectively. The review concluded that neutrophils predominated in the airways of children with RSV. The findings emphasize the need for further research into the implications of these immune responses on long-term health outcomes.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述旨在调查呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)感染儿童气道炎症中占主导地位的细胞类型,重点关注免疫应答在长期并发症中的作用。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 综述包括系统搜索PubMed、Embase、Google Scholar和Web of Science,截至2025年8月31日,搜索英文发表的研究。使用Joanna Briggs Institute批判性评估检查表进行偏倚评估。对涉及202例RSV感染儿童和97例未感染对照的6项研究进行了荟萃分析。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 荟萃分析发现,RSV感染儿童的支气管肺泡灌洗液中中性粒细胞百分比增加,巨噬细胞百分比减少。森林图显示中性粒细胞和巨噬细胞百分比的合并标准化均数差和95%置信区间分别为2.12(1.74至2.50)和−3.14(−4.16至−2.12)。综述结论指出,RSV感染儿童的气道中以中性粒细胞为主。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 综述指出,I2值超过40%表明研究之间存在异质性。然而,提供的证据未报告与发现相关的具体争议或未解决的机制。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 研究结果强调了未来研究和临床实践中调查RSV诱导的气道炎症中中性粒细胞作用的重要性。综述表明,需要进一步研究探索这些免疫应答对长期并发症的含义。

papers.title: Bivalent RSVpreF Effectiveness Against Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)-Related Respiratory Disease Hospitalization and Emergency Department Visits Across Three RSV Seasons.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) protein subunit vaccines reduce the risk of severe outcomes such as hospitalization and emergency department (ED) visits for at least two RSV seasons following vaccination. No data have been published on real-world RSV vaccine effectiveness (VE) beyond the second season after vaccination. This study evaluates bivalent RSVpreF VE against RSV-related respiratory disease hospitalizations/ED visits throughout three seasons after vaccination. METHODS: This retrospective test-negative case-control study evaluates bivalent RSVpreF VE among adults aged ≥60 years at Kaiser Permanente Southern California, USA, with lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) or acute respiratory illness (ARI) over three RSV seasons (11/24/2023-4/18/2026). Cases were RSV-positive without coinfection. Controls were negative for RSV, hMPV, influenza, SARS-CoV-2, and positive for a non-vaccine preventable disease pathogen. Exposure was bivalent RSVpreF (Abrysvo) receipt ≥ 21 days before LRTD/ARI. Adjusted VE was estimated using odds ratios from multivariable logistic regression or generalized estimating equations. RESULTS: Overall adjusted VE against RSV-related LRTD hospitalization/ED visits was 80% (95% CI 68-87), 70% (95% CI 53-81), and 51% (95% CI -12-78) in the first, second, and third season after vaccination, respectively. Overall adjusted VE against RSV-related ARI hospitalization/ED visits was 81% (71-87), 64% (48-75), and 60% (15-81), respectively. Adjusted VE among non-immunocompromised individuals trended 4-7% higher than corresponding overall estimates. Overall adjusted VE across the three combined seasons was 73% (95% CI 64-80) and 73% (95% CI 65-79) against RSV-related LRTD and ARI, respectively. CONCLUSION: Bivalent RSVpreF provides protection against RSV-related respiratory hospitalization/ED visits for at least three seasons after vaccination in this population of older adults with a high prevalence of comorbidities. Estimates in the third season for ARI were more definitive, while those for LRTD were imprecise due to limited event numbers. This suggests bivalent RSVpreF vaccination results in substantial individual and public health benefit. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT06077968.

papers.title: Burden of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) hospitalizations among adults aged 60 years or more in Brazil: A retrospective surveillance database analysis (2013-2024).
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Globally, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of severe respiratory illness in adults aged ≥60 years. Risk increases with advancing age and comorbidities, particularly cardiopulmonary disease and diabetes. RSV disease burden in adults is often underestimated due to non-specific presentation and limited testing. In Brazil, RSV is a recognized driver of hospitalizations and deaths in older adults, yet comprehensive epidemiological data remain scarce. Here, we describe RSV-associated severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) hospitalizations among adults aged ≥60 years in Brazil between 2013 and 2024. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed RSV-associated SARI hospitalizations reported to the national Influenza Epidemiological Surveillance Information System -Gripe. Outcomes included hospitalization frequency, in-hospital mortality, case fatality rates (CFRs), seasonality, healthcare resource utilization, and comorbidities. RESULTS: Between 2013 and 2024, 4,636 RSV-related hospitalizations occurred in adults aged ≥60 years, increasing sharply after the COVID-19 pandemic (2020-2024). Hospitalization rates increased from 15 per 100,000 in 2024. Women accounted for most cases (59%), and hospitalizations were concentrated in the South and Southeast regions partly due to test availability. In-hospital mortality increased over time, with mean rates nearly fivefold higher post-pandemic than pre-pandemic. CFRs remained consistently high (21-31%), particularly in adults aged ≥80 years. The mean length of hospital stay was 12.9 days. Almost one-third of cases required intensive care unit admission, of whom more than two-thirds needed ventilatory support. Comorbidities were present in 71% of cases, most commonly cardiovascular (65%) and diabetes (33%)were strongly associated with increased mortality and healthcare resource utilization. CONCLUSIONS: RSV poses a substantial and increasing burden among Brazilian adults aged ≥60 years, with a high CFR, prolonged hospitalizations, and intensive healthcare resource utilization. These findings highlight the need to strengthen RSV surveillance and discuss vaccination strategies for adults aged older in Brazil.

Risk increases with advancing age and comorbidities, particularly cardiopulmonary disease and diabetes. RSV disease burden in adults is often underestimated due to non-specific presentation and limited testing. In Brazil, RSV is a recognized driver of hospitalizations and deaths in older adults, yet comprehensive epidemiological data remain scarce. Here, we describe RSV-associated severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) hospitalizations among adults aged ≥60 years in Brazil between 2013 and 2024. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed RSV-associated SARI hospitalizations reported to the national Influenza Epidemiological Surveillance Information System -Gripe. Outcomes included hospitalization frequency, in-hospital mortality, case fatality rates (CFRs), seasonality, healthcare resource utilization, and comorbidities. RESULTS: Between 2013 and 2024, 4,636 RSV-related hospitalizations occurred in adults aged ≥60 years, increasing sharply after the COVID-19 pandemic (2020-2024). Hospitalization rates increased from 15 per 100,000 in 2024. Women accounted for most cases (59%), and hospitalizations were concentrated in the South and Southeast regions partly due to test availability. In-hospital mortality increased over time, with mean rates nearly fivefold higher post-pandemic than pre-pandemic. CFRs remained consistently high (21-31%), particularly in adults aged ≥80 years. The mean length of hospital stay was 12.9 days. Almost one-third of cases required intensive care unit admission, of whom more than two-thirds needed ventilatory support. Comorbidities were present in 71% of cases, most commonly cardiovascular (65%) and diabetes (33%)were strongly associated with increased mortality and healthcare resource utilization. CONCLUSIONS: RSV poses a substantial and increasing burden among Brazilian adults aged ≥60 years, with a high CFR, prolonged hospitalizations, and intensive healthcare resource utilization. These findings highlight the need to strengthen RSV surveillance and discuss vaccination strategies for adults aged older in Brazil.

papers.title: Bardoxolone methyl exerts an inhibitory effect on respiratory syncytial virus infection by downregulating IL-6 via the IKKβ/NF-κB signaling pathway.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals, but therapeutic options for active infection remain limited. Interleukin-6 (IL-6) contributes to RSV replication and RSV-induced inflammation, and the IKKβ/NF-κB pathway is a major regulator of IL-6 expression. Bardoxolone methyl (BXM) was identified by network medicine as a potential anti-RSV compound, with molecular docking suggesting interactions with the IKKβ/NF-κB pathway. We investigated whether BXM inhibits RSV infection through modulation of the IKKβ/NF-κB/IL-6 axis in RSV-infected BEAS-2B cells and BALB/c mice. RSV infection increased IL-6 expression and activated IKKβ/NF-κB signaling, whereas IL-6 knockdown reduced viral replication and inflammatory mediator expression. BXM significantly suppressed RSV replication, as shown by RT-qPCR, TCID50, plaque reduction assays, and Western blotting, and decreased IL-6 expression in vitro . Mechanistically, BXM attenuated RSV-induced phosphorylation of IKKβ and NF-κB. The IKKβ inhibitor TPCA-1 produced similar inhibitory effects, whereas recombinant human IL-6 add-back partially restored inflammatory mediator expression in BXM-treated RSV-infected cells. In mice, BXM reduced lung viral titers, RSV-F expression, IL-6 expression, IKKβ/NF-κB activation, and RSV-induced lung injury. These findings suggest that BXM suppresses RSV replication and inflammation, at least in part, by modulating the IKKβ/NF-κB/IL-6 axis, supporting its potential as a therapeutic candidate for RSV infection. IMPORTANCE Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of respiratory illness, especially in infants, older adults, and people with weakened immune systems. Although preventive strategies are available for some high-risk groups, treatment options for active RSV infection remain limited. This study identifies bardoxolone methyl (BXM) as a potential anti-RSV compound and shows that it can reduce both viral replication and virus-induced inflammation in cell and mouse models. Importantly, our findings suggest that BXM acts, at least in part, by reducing IL-6-related inflammatory signaling, which is closely associated with RSV disease severity. These results provide experimental evidence supporting BXM as a promising candidate for further development against RSV infection and offer insight into a potential host-targeted therapeutic strategy.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)会导致婴儿、老年人和免疫功能低下人群的严重下呼吸道感染,但针对活动性感染的治疗选择仍然有限。白细胞介素-6(IL-6)促进RSV复制和RSV引发的炎症,而IKKβ/NF-κB通路是调控IL-6表达的主要途径。甲基巴多昔芬(BXM)通过网络医学被鉴定为一种潜在的抗RSV化合物,分子对接研究表明其与IKKβ/NF-κB通路存在相互作用。我们研究了BXM是否通过调节RSV感染的BEAS-2B细胞和BALB/c小鼠中的IKKβ/NF-κB/IL-6轴来抑制RSV感染。RSV感染会增加IL-6表达并激活IKKβ/NF-κB信号通路,而IL-6敲低则会减少病毒复制和炎症介质的表达。BXM在体外显著抑制了RSV复制,如RT-qPCR、TCID50、斑块减少实验和Western blotting所示,并降低了IL-6的表达。从机制上看,BXM减弱了RSV诱导的IKKβ和NF-κB的磷酸化。IKKβ抑制剂TPCA-1产生了类似的抑制效果,而重组人IL-6添加则部分恢复了BXM处理的RSV感染细胞中炎症介质的表达。在小鼠中,BXM降低了肺部病毒滴度、RSV-F表达、IL-6表达、IKKβ/NF-κB激活以及RSV诱导的肺损伤。这些发现表明,BXM通过调节IKKβ/NF-κB/IL-6轴抑制RSV复制和炎症,支持其作为RSV感染治疗候选药物的潜力。重要性 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是导致呼吸道疾病的主要原因之一,尤其是在婴儿、老年人和免疫功能低下人群中。尽管某些高危群体已有预防策略,但针对活动性RSV感染的治疗选择仍然有限。本研究确定了甲基巴多昔芬(BXM)作为潜在的抗RSV化合物,并表明其在细胞和小鼠模型中可以减少病毒复制和病毒诱导的炎症。重要的是,我们的发现表明,BXM至少部分通过减少与IL-6相关的炎症信号发挥作用,而这些信号与RSV疾病的严重程度密切相关。这些结果为BXM作为对抗RSV感染的潜在候选药物提供了实验依据,并为针对宿主的治疗策略提供了见解。

papers.title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)–An Urgent Priority in Respiratory Disease Prevention
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract disease in infants, young children, older adults, and individuals with cardiopulmonary comorbidities or immunocompromised states. Recent advances enable layered prevention through maternal vaccination for infant protection, long-acting monoclonal antibodies for newborns and select toddlers, and vaccines for older adults. However, inequities in surveillance, seasonality-driven timing, and challenges in affordability and delivery—particularly in low- and middle-income countries— impede equitable uptake. This editorial underscores priority populations, synthesizes current evidence and policy directions, and outlines actionable levers in financing, procurement, and integrated maternal–child health delivery to accelerate access, making RSV prevention an urgent and achievable global health priority.

papers.title: Molecular detection of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in hospitalized children at the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville, Republic of the Congo
papers.abstract: Epidemiological Respiratory viral infections are among the most common diseases responsible for morbidity and mortality among children in sub-Saharan Africa, with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) being a major contributor. This situation highlights the urgent need for rapid and accurate diagnostic tools. The objective of this study was to detect RSV among hospitalized children under five years of age with acute respiratory infections at the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville in the Republic of the Congo. A total of 81 nasopharyngeal swab samples were collected from children aged ≤5 years who were admitted to the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit and Neonatology Department of the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville with acute respiratory infections between August and December 2023. Respiratory viruses were identified using rapid antigen detection assays and reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). Rapid antigen tests detected SARS-CoV-2 in 2 cases (2.5%), whereas RSV and influenza A and B were not detected. In contrast, RT-qPCR identified RSV in 4 samples (4.9%). All RSV-positive patients were male, aged over 28 days, and hospitalized in the pediatric intensive care unit. The main clinical signs observed were respiratory distress (100%), cough (75%), fever (50%) and rhinorrhea (50%). These findings confirm the circulation of RSV among hospitalized children at the University Hospital Center of Brazzaville and highlight the superior sensitivity of RT-qPCR over rapid antigen tests for RSV detection. Key words: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), children, rapid antigen test, reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), Brazzaville.

papers.abstract_zh: 流行病学呼吸道病毒感染是撒哈拉以南非洲儿童发病率和死亡率的主要原因之一,其中呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是主要贡献者。这一情况凸显了快速准确诊断工具的迫切需求。本研究的目的是检测刚果共和国布拉扎维尔大学医院中心住院的5岁以下急性呼吸道感染儿童中的RSV。2023年8月至12月期间,从布拉扎维尔大学医院中心儿科重症监护室和新生儿科收治的年龄≤5岁的儿童中收集了81份鼻咽拭子样本。使用快速抗原检测试验和逆转录定量聚合酶链反应(RT-qPCR)鉴定呼吸道病毒。快速抗原检测试验在2例(2.5%)中检测到SARS-CoV-2,而RSV和流感A、B型病毒均未被检测到。相比之下,RT-qPCR在4份样本(4.9%)中检测到RSV。所有RSV阳性患者均为男性,年龄超过28天,并住院在儿科重症监护室。观察到的主要临床症状包括呼吸窘迫(100%)、咳嗽(75%)、发热(50%)和流涕(50%)。这些发现证实了RSV在刚果共和国布拉扎维尔大学医院中心住院儿童中的流行,并突显了RT-qPCR在RSV检测中相较于快速抗原检测试验的更高灵敏度。关键词:呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)、儿童、快速抗原检测、逆转录定量聚合酶链反应(RT-qPCR)、布拉扎维尔。

papers.title: Post-pandemic re-establishment of respiratory virus seasonality and molecular epidemiology of Rhinovirus/Enterovirus in Northern Italy: a three-year surveillance study (2023-2026).
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Following the COVID-19 pandemic, respiratory virus circulation progressively returned towards patterns observed in the pre-pandemic period. However, long-term epidemiological data describing the re-establishment of respiratory viral seasonality and the molecular diversity of Rhinovirus/Enterovirus (RV/EV) remain limited. METHODS: To investigate the circulation patterns of respiratory viruses and characterize the RV/EV in Northern Italy, a retrospective observational study was conducted on samples collected between April 2023 and April 2026 at Brescia Civic Hospital. Respiratory viruses were detected by real-time PCR, and RV/EV-positive samples were characterized through next-generation sequencing. RESULTS: A total of 6,919 respiratory virus-positive samples were identified. SARS-CoV-2 remained the most frequently detected pathogen, followed by RV/EV, influenza A/B (FLU A/B), adenovirus, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), parainfluenza virus, bocavirus, and human metapneumovirus. Distinct seasonal peaks were observed for FLU A/B and RSV during winter months, whereas RV/EV circulated continuously throughout the year. Molecular characterization of 224 RV/EV-positive samples revealed substantial genetic diversity. Pediatric patients accounted for the majority of sequenced cases. CONCLUSIONS: Three years after the end of the COVID-19 pandemic, respiratory viruses have re-established their characteristic seasonal circulation patterns. Nevertheless, RV/EV remain the dominant non-influenza respiratory pathogens and display considerable genetic heterogeneity. Continuous molecular surveillance is essential for early detection of emerging respiratory viral threats.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to investigate the re-establishment of respiratory virus seasonality and molecular diversity of Rhinovirus/Enterovirus (RV/EV) in Northern Italy following the COVID-19 pandemic. Conducted at Brescia Civic Hospital between April 2023 and April 2026, the study used real-time PCR to detect respiratory viruses and next-generation sequencing to characterize RV/EV. Molecular characterization of 224 RV/EV-positive samples revealed substantial genetic diversity, with pediatric patients accounting for the majority of sequenced cases. The authors concluded that respiratory viruses have re-established their seasonal patterns three years post-pandemic. They emphasized the importance of continuous molecular surveillance for detecting emerging threats. However, they noted that RV/EV remain dominant non-influenza respiratory pathogens with significant genetic heterogeneity, highlighting the need for further research.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: Following the COVID-19 pandemic, respiratory virus circulation progressively returned towards patterns observed in the pre-pandemic period. elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 为研究呼吸道病毒的传播模式并分析北意大利地区的RV/EV,我们在布雷西亚市民医院收集了2023年4月至2026年4月期间的样本,并进行了回顾性观察研究。
elements_zh.methods: 呼吸道病毒通过实时PCR检测,RV/EV阳性样本通过下一代测序进行特征分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 共鉴定出6,919例呼吸道病毒阳性样本。SARS-CoV-2仍然是最常检测到的病原体,其次是RV/EV、流感A/B(FLU A/B)、腺病毒、呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)、副流感病毒、博卡病毒和人偏肺病毒。在冬季观察到FLU A/B和RSV的明显季节性高峰,而RV/EV全年持续传播。对224例RV/EV阳性样本的分子特征分析显示存在显著的遗传多样性。儿童患者占了大多数的测序病例。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: Three years after the end of the COVID-19 pandemic, respiratory viruses have re-established their characteristic seasonal circulation patterns.
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 持续的分子监测对于早期发现新兴呼吸道病毒威胁至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 然而,RV/EV仍然是主要的非流感呼吸道病原体,并表现出显著的遗传异质性。

papers.source_body_en: OBJECTIVES: Following the COVID-19 pandemic, respiratory virus circulation progressively returned towards patterns observed in the pre-pandemic period. However, long-term epidemiological data describing the re-establishment of respiratory viral seasonality and the molecular diversity of Rhinovirus/Enterovirus (RV/EV) remain limited. METHODS: To investigate the circulation patterns of respiratory viruses and characterize the RV/EV in Northern Italy, a retrospective observational study was conducted on samples collected between April 2023 and April 2026 at Brescia Civic Hospital. Respiratory viruses were detected by real-time PCR, and RV/EV-positive samples were characterized through next-generation sequencing. RESULTS: A total of 6,919 respiratory virus-positive samples were identified. SARS-CoV-2 remained the most frequently detected pathogen, followed by RV/EV, influenza A/B (FLU A/B), adenovirus, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), parainfluenza virus, bocavirus, and human metapneumovirus. Distinct seasonal peaks were observed for FLU A/B and RSV during winter months, whereas RV/EV circulated continuously throughout the year. Molecular characterization of 224 RV/EV-positive samples revealed substantial genetic diversity. Pediatric patients accounted for the majority of sequenced cases. CONCLUSIONS: Three years after the end of the COVID-19 pandemic, respiratory viruses have re-established their characteristic seasonal circulation patterns. Nevertheless, RV/EV remain the dominant non-influenza respiratory pathogens and display considerable genetic heterogeneity. Continuous molecular surveillance is essential for early detection of emerging respiratory viral threats.

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 为研究呼吸道病毒的传播模式并分析北意大利地区的RV/EV,我们在布雷西亚市民医院收集了2023年4月至2026年4月期间的样本,并进行了回顾性观察研究。
analysis_zh.methods: 呼吸道病毒通过实时PCR检测,RV/EV阳性样本通过下一代测序进行特征分析。
analysis_zh.main_results: 共鉴定出6,919例呼吸道病毒阳性样本。SARS-CoV-2仍然是最常检测到的病原体,其次是RV/EV、流感A/B(FLU A/B)、腺病毒、呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)、副流感病毒、博卡病毒和人偏肺病毒。在冬季观察到FLU A/B和RSV的明显季节性高峰,而RV/EV全年持续传播。对224例RV/EV阳性样本的分子特征分析显示存在显著的遗传多样性。儿童患者占了大多数的测序病例。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 持续的分子监测对于早期发现新兴呼吸道病毒威胁至关重要。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 然而,RV/EV仍然是主要的非流感呼吸道病原体,并表现出显著的遗传异质性。

papers.title: RESPIRATORY SYNCYTIAL VIRUS INFECTION IN PATIENTS WITH RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS: DOES DISEASE STATUS AND IMMUNOSUPPRESSION ALTER CLINICAL COURSE, SEVERITY, AND HOSPITALIZATION RISK?
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is an increasingly recognized cause of severe respiratory infection in older adults, particularly those with underlying comorbidities and immunosuppression. However, the specific burden of RSV disease in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and other systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARD) remains incompletely characterized. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on RSV epidemiology in immunocompromised populations, pathophysiological mechanisms underlying increased susceptibility in RA, risk stratification approaches, clinical presentation and complications, prevention strategies including recently approved vaccines (Arexvy, Abrysvo, mResvia), and clinical management recommendations. Recent data demonstrate that RA patients have substantially higher hospitalization rates (approximately 54%) compared with immunocompetent older adults (6–8%), with frailty emerging as the strongest independent predictor of severe infection (adjusted odds ratio 5.15). Contemporary evidence supports the benefit of RSV vaccination in older adults; however, reduced immunogenicity has been documented in patients receiving targeted immunosuppressive therapies. This review emphasizes individualized risk assessment, optimization of immunosuppression, timely vaccination with enhanced monitoring in high-risk subgroups, early clinical recognition of RSV infection, and evidence-based management approaches. By integrating clinical epidemiology with preventive and therapeutic strategies, contemporary practice can substantially reduce RSV-related complications in this vulnerable population.

analysis.scope_and_question: This review focuses on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA), examining whether disease status and immunosuppression alter clinical course, severity, and hospitalization risk.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of current evidence on RSV epidemiology in immunocompromised populations, pathophysiological mechanisms, risk stratification, clinical presentation, prevention strategies, and management recommendations. It does not report specific databases, search dates, or meta-analysis methods.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: RA patients have substantially higher hospitalization rates for RSV infection (approximately 54%) compared with immunocompetent older adults (6–8%), with frailty being the strongest independent predictor of severe infection (adjusted odds ratio 5.15). Contemporary evidence supports the benefit of RSV vaccination in older adults, though reduced immunogenicity has been documented in patients receiving targeted immunosuppressive therapies.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights that the specific burden of RSV disease in RA patients remains incompletely characterized. There is a lack of detailed data on the effectiveness of RSV vaccines in RA patients and the precise mechanisms of increased susceptibility to RSV in this population.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the need for individualized risk assessment, optimization of immunosuppression, timely vaccination with enhanced monitoring in high-risk subgroups, early clinical recognition of RSV infection, and evidence-based management approaches.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the impact of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and immunosuppression on the clinical course, severity, and hospitalization risk of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection. It synthesizes current evidence on RSV epidemiology, pathophysiology, risk stratification, and management strategies in immunocompromised populations. The findings indicate that RA patients have significantly higher hospitalization rates for RSV compared to immunocompetent individuals, with frailty identified as a key predictor of severe outcomes. While RSV vaccination is beneficial for older adults, reduced immunogenicity in RA patients receiving immunosuppressive therapies is noted. The review underscores the importance of individualized risk assessment, optimized immunosuppression, and targeted vaccination strategies for high-risk subgroups. However, the specific burden of RSV in RA remains incompletely characterized, highlighting the need for further research and improved surveillance.

analysis_en.scope_and_question: This review focuses on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA), examining whether disease status and immunosuppression alter clinical course, severity, and hospitalization risk.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of current evidence on RSV epidemiology in immunocompromised populations, pathophysiological mechanisms, risk stratification, clinical presentation, prevention strategies, and management recommendations. It does not report specific databases, search dates, or meta-analysis methods.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: RA patients have substantially higher hospitalization rates for RSV infection (approximately 54%) compared with immunocompetent older adults (6–8%), with frailty being the strongest independent predictor of severe infection (adjusted odds ratio 5.15). analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights that the specific burden of RSV disease in RA patients remains incompletely characterized. papers.title_zh: 类风湿关节炎患者呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)感染:疾病状态和免疫抑制是否改变临床过程、严重程度和住院风险?
papers.source_body_en: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is an increasingly recognized cause of severe respiratory infection in older adults, particularly those with underlying comorbidities and immunosuppression. However, the specific burden of RSV disease in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and other systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARD) remains incompletely characterized. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on RSV epidemiology in immunocompromised populations, pathophysiological mechanisms underlying increased susceptibility in RA, risk stratification approaches, clinical presentation and complications, prevention strategies including recently approved vaccines (Arexvy, Abrysvo, mResvia), and clinical management recommendations. Recent data demonstrate that RA patients have substantially higher hospitalization rates (approximately 54%) compared with immunocompetent older adults (6–8%), with frailty emerging as the strongest independent predictor of severe infection (adjusted odds ratio 5.15). Contemporary evidence supports the benefit of RSV vaccination in older adults; however, reduced immunogenicity has been documented in patients receiving targeted immunosuppressive therapies. This review emphasizes individualized risk assessment, optimization of immunosuppression, timely vaccination with enhanced monitoring in high-risk subgroups, early clinical recognition of RSV infection, and evidence-based management approaches. By integrating clinical epidemiology with preventive and therapeutic strategies, contemporary practice can substantially reduce RSV-related complications in this vulnerable population.
papers.abstract_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)是老年人群中日益被认可的严重呼吸道感染原因之一,尤其是那些有基础合并症和免疫抑制的患者。然而,RSV感染在类风湿关节炎(RA)和其他系统性自身免疫风湿性疾病(SARD)患者中的具体负担仍不完全明确。本叙述性综述综合了当前关于RSV在免疫缺陷人群中感染的证据,探讨了RA患者中增加易感性的病理生理机制,风险分层方法,临床表现和并发症,预防策略包括最近获批的尼塞韦单抗(Arexvy,Abrysvo,mResvia),以及临床管理建议。最新数据显示,RA患者RSV感染的住院率显著高于免疫功能正常的老年人(约54% vs 6–8%),而虚弱是严重感染最强的独立预测因素(调整比值比5.15)。当前证据支持在老年人群中使用RSV疫苗的益处;然而,在接受靶向免疫抑制治疗的患者中,已记录到疫苗免疫原性降低的现象。本综述强调个体化风险评估、免疫抑制优化、在高风险亚组中及时接种疫苗并加强监测、早期识别RSV感染以及基于证据的管理方法。通过将临床数据与预防和治疗策略相结合,现代实践可以显著减少这一易感人群的RSV相关并发症。

papers.title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine Effectiveness Among US Older Adults, 2023-2024 Season
papers.abstract: Importance: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes a substantial number of hospitalizations and deaths among older adults. Two RSV vaccines for individuals aged 60 years or older were approved in 2023; it was important to monitor their clinical effectiveness during routine care in the first RSV season after regulatory approval. Objective: To estimate the clinical effectiveness of RSV vaccines during routine care overall and by brand among US older adults. Design, Setting, and Participants: This nationally representative, retrospective cohort study evaluated the effectiveness of RSV vaccines from August 6, 2023, to March 2, 2024. The primary analysis included eligible Medicare fee-for-service beneficiaries aged 65 years or older. Exposures: The RSVPreF3+AS01 RSV vaccine (GSK) and RSVpreF RSV vaccine (Pfizer). Main Outcomes and Measures: RSV-related hospitalization and RSV-related death. Results: Among 14 819 226 unvaccinated beneficiaries at the beginning of the study, the median age was 74 years (IQR, 70-79 years) and 57.7% were female. By the study end date, 13.9% of beneficiaries had received a RSVPreF3+AS01 vaccine, and 6.4% received a RSVpreF vaccine. Compared with the unvaccinated cohort, vaccinated individuals were less likely to have low-income status, lived in more affluent areas, and were more likely to have prior influenza vaccination and prior COVID-19 vaccination. The RSVPreF3+AS01 and RSVpreF vaccinated cohorts were largely comparable in demographic, social, and medical characteristics. Overall estimated vaccine effectiveness compared with the unvaccinated cohort was 81.8% (95% CI, 80.0%-83.4%) against RSV-related hospitalization and 85.0% (95% CI, 75.1%-90.9%) against RSV-related death. Brand-specific vaccine effectiveness against RSV-related hospitalization was 79.9% (95% CI, 77.6%-81.9%) for RSVPreF3+AS01 and 85.1% (95% CI, 82.2%-87.5%) for RSVpreF compared with the unvaccinated cohort. Vaccine effectiveness against RSV-related hospitalization was 72.2% (95% CI, 67.4%-76.3%) for immunocompromised individuals. Effectiveness did not change significantly with age. Conclusions and Relevance: In this cohort study of US older adults, both RSVPreF3+AS01 and RSVpreF vaccines had high effectiveness against RSV-related hospitalization and death during the 2023-2024 season. RSV vaccines demonstrated substantial effectiveness within this high-risk older adult population, including among immunocompromised individuals and across all ages 65 years or older. This large postmarketing noninterventional study provides clinical evidence of RSV vaccine effectiveness in the first year of vaccine approval.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the clinical effectiveness of two RSV vaccines, RSVPreF3+AS01 (GSK) and RSVpreF (Pfizer), among US older adults during the 2023-2024 season. The research is motivated by the significant burden of RSV-related hospitalizations and deaths in this population and the need to monitor vaccine performance post-approval. A nationally representative, retrospective cohort study design was used, analyzing Medicare fee-for-service beneficiaries aged 65 years or older. The study found that overall vaccine effectiveness against RSV-related hospitalization was 81.8% (95% CI, 80.0%-83.4%) and against RSV-related death was 85.0% (95% CI, 75.1%-90.9%). Brand-specific effectiveness was 79.9% (95% CI, 77.6%-81.9%) for RSVPreF3+AS01 and 85.1% (95% CI, 82.2%-87.5%) for RSVpreF. Immunocompromised individuals showed 72.2% (95% CI, 67.4%-76.3%) effectiveness against hospitalization, and effectiveness did not vary significantly with age. The study highlights the substantial effectiveness of RSV vaccines in older adults, including those at higher risk, and provides important postmarketing evidence for vaccine use. However, the retrospective design may introduce biases, limiting the strength of the evidence to moderate.

papers.title: Adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccine impact over three respiratory syncytial virus seasons in older adults with comorbidities.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: We explored the efficacy of AS01E-adjuvanted respiratory syncytial virus prefusion F protein-based vaccine (adjuvanted RSVPreF3) in subpopulations of participants with underlying medical conditions in the multi-country, phase 3 AReSVi-006 trial (conducted between May 2021 and May 2024). METHODS: Medically stable ≥60-year-olds were 1:1-randomised to receive one adjuvanted RSVPreF3 or placebo dose pre-RSV season 1. In exploratory post hoc analyses in subgroups of participants with underlying conditions (including COPD, asthma, diabetes and obesity (body mass index ≥30 kg·m-2)), we evaluated efficacy of one vaccine dose against RSV-related lower respiratory tract disease (RSV-LRTD), RSV-related acute respiratory illness (RSV-ARI) and RSV-ARI-related complications (e.g., pneumonia, COPD/asthma exacerbation and cardiovascular events). We also evaluated (post hoc) RSV-ARI-related systemic corticosteroid and antibiotics use in participants with COPD or asthma. RESULTS: The efficacy analyses comprised 12 468 vaccine and 12 498 placebo recipients. Efficacy against RSV-LRTD over three RSV seasons was similar among participants with COPD (75.1%, 95% CI: 40.2-91.4), asthma (65.8%, 31.0-84.7), diabetes (69.8%, 37.5-87.1) and obesity (74.1%, 56.4-85.5) as in the overall study population (62.9%, 97.5% CI: 46.7-74.8). Efficacy was also observed against RSV-ARI in these subgroups. Efficacy against RSV-ARI-related complications was 74.4% (95% CI: 11.2-95.2) in participants with COPD and 60.8% (-9.9-88.7) in those with asthma. Among participants with COPD, 15.4% (1.9-45.4) of RSV-ARI episodes in vaccine versus 22.4% (12.5-35.3) in placebo recipients were treated with systemic corticosteroids, and 46.2% (19.2-74.9) versus 56.9% (43.2-69.8) with antibiotics. CONCLUSIONS: Post hoc analyses of the AReSVi-006 trial suggest that adjuvanted RSVPreF3 may help prevent RSV-ARI, RSV-LRTD and RSV-related complications in medically stable older adults with underlying medical conditions like COPD and asthma.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of the adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccine in older adults with comorbidities during three RSV seasons, addressing the need for targeted prevention strategies in high-risk populations.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was a multi-country, phase 3 AReSVi-006 trial conducted between May 2021 and May 2024, randomising medically stable ≥60-year-olds in a 1:1 ratio to receive one dose of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 or placebo pre-RSV season.
analysis.methods: Participants were randomised to receive one dose of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 or placebo, and post hoc analyses were conducted to assess vaccine efficacy against RSV-related lower respiratory tract disease, RSV-related acute respiratory illness, and related complications in subgroups with underlying conditions such as COPD, asthma, diabetes, and obesity.
analysis.main_results: Efficacy against RSV-LRTD over three RSV seasons was similar across subgroups with COPD (75.1%, 95% CI: 40.2-91.4), asthma (65.8%, 31.0-84.7), diabetes (69.8%, 37.5-87.1), and obesity (74.1%, 56.4-85.5) as in the overall study population (62.9%, 97.5% CI: 46.7-74.8).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccine may be effective in preventing RSV-ARI, RSV-LRTD, and RSV-related complications in medically stable older adults with underlying medical conditions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide evidence for the potential use of the adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccine in preventing RSV-related illnesses in high-risk older adults, which could inform future vaccination strategies for this population.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on post hoc analyses, which may introduce bias, and the efficacy against RSV-ARI-related complications showed wide confidence intervals, suggesting moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the efficacy of the adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccine in older adults with comorbidities during three RSV seasons. The multi-country, phase 3 AReSVi-006 trial randomised medically stable participants aged ≥60 years to receive one dose of the vaccine or placebo. Post hoc analyses showed similar efficacy against RSV-LRTD across subgroups with COPD, asthma, diabetes, and obesity as in the overall population. Efficacy against RSV-ARI was also observed in these subgroups. The study suggests the vaccine may help prevent RSV-ARI, RSV-LRTD, and related complications in high-risk older adults. However, the findings are based on post hoc analyses, which may introduce bias, and the confidence intervals for efficacy against RSV-ARI-related complications were wide, indicating moderate evidence strength.

papers.title_zh: 佐剂修饰的RSVPreF3 疫苗在有合并症的老年人中连续三个呼吸道合胞病毒季节的疗效影响。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: We explored the efficacy of AS01E-adjuvanted respiratory syncytial virus prefusion F protein-based vaccine (adjuvanted RSVPreF3) in subpopulations of participants with underlying medical conditions in the multi-country, phase 3 AReSVi-006 trial (conducted between May 2021 and May 2024). METHODS: Medically stable ≥60-year-olds were 1:1-randomised to receive one adjuvanted RSVPreF3 or placebo dose pre-RSV season 1. In exploratory post hoc analyses in subgroups of participants with underlying conditions (including COPD, asthma, diabetes and obesity (body mass index ≥30 kg·m-2)), we evaluated efficacy of one vaccine dose against RSV-related lower respiratory tract disease (RSV-LRTD), RSV-related acute respiratory illness (RSV-ARI) and RSV-ARI-related complications (e.g., pneumonia, COPD/asthma exacerbation and cardiovascular events). We also evaluated (post hoc) RSV-ARI-related systemic corticosteroid and antibiotics use in participants with COPD or asthma. RESULTS: The efficacy analyses comprised 12 468 vaccine and 12 498 placebo recipients. Efficacy against RSV-LRTD over three RSV seasons was similar among participants with COPD (75.1%, 95% CI: 40.2-91.4), asthma (65.8%, 31.0-84.7), diabetes (69.8%, 37.5-87.1) and obesity (74.1%, 56.4-85.5) as in the overall study population (62.9%, 97.5% CI: 46.7-74.8). Efficacy was also observed against RSV-ARI in these subgroups. Efficacy against RSV-ARI-related complications was 74.4% (95% CI: 11.2-95.2) in participants with COPD and 60.8% (-9.9-88.7) in those with asthma. Among participants with COPD, 15.4% (1.9-45.4) of RSV-ARI episodes in vaccine versus 22.4% (12.5-35.3) in placebo recipients were treated with systemic corticosteroids, and 46.2% (19.2-74.9) versus 56.9% (43.2-69.8) with antibiotics. CONCLUSIONS: Post hoc analyses of the AReSVi-006 trial suggest that adjuvanted RSVPreF3 may help prevent RSV-ARI, RSV-LRTD and RSV-related complications in medically stable older adults with underlying medical conditions like COPD and asthma.

papers.title: Viral Metagenomic Sequencing Reveals Viral Codetection Patterns in Children with Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of pediatric respiratory infections, yet the frequency and composition of viral codetections in affected children have not been extensively profiled using unbiased sequencing approaches. Here, we performed viral metagenomic sequencing on nasopharyngeal swabs collected from 42 pediatric patients with confirmed RSV infection to characterize the codetection landscape. RSV was detected and genotyped in all specimens. Beyond RSV, we identified nine additional human respiratory viruses coexisting across the cohort; several of these fall outside the scope of routine diagnostic panels, although their clinical significance remains uncertain. Codetections were the rule rather than the exception: 30 of 42 samples harbored at least three viruses, with up to seven distinct viruses detected in a single case. These findings underscore the taxonomic breadth and polymicrobial complexity of respiratory infections in children. Our results describe the viral codetection landscape in RSV-infected children, revealing a broader spectrum of co-occurring viruses than typically captured by targeted diagnostics, although the clinical significance of most codetections remains uncertain. These findings highlight the polymicrobial complexity of RSV infections and underscore the need for prospective studies to determine which codetections are clinically meaningful.

papers.title: Characteristics and outcomes of adult patients hospitalised with RSV infection, influenza or COVID-19 in Belgium, winter seasons 2023/24 and 2024/25
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) cause substantial disease burden in older adults and those with comorbidities. AIM To inform Belgian vaccination policies, we aimed to compare risk profiles and outcomes of influenza, COVID-19 and RSV infections and examine age-related differences. METHODS Adults (≥ 18 years) hospitalised with SARI in nine Belgian sentinel hospitals during the 2023/24 and 2024/25 winter seasons were included. Patients with laboratory-confirmed RSV infection, influenza or COVID-19 were compared in terms of demographics, comorbidities, complications and outcomes. Adults 18–64 years were compared with those ≥ 65 years. Multivariate analyses were applied. RESULTS Among 2,806 patients, 535 (19.1%) had RSV infection, 1,694 (60.4%) influenza and 577 (20.6%) COVID-19. Patients with influenza were significantly younger (mean age 68.9 years) and had significantly fewer comorbidities (89.7%) than patients with RSV (73.8 years; 95.8%) or COVID-19 (74.0 years; 93.6%). Patients with COVID-19 experienced significantly fewer complications (40.8%) than patients with RSV (48.9%) or influenza (45.2%). Patients with RSV had higher in-hospital mortality (11.9%) than patients with influenza (7.3%; p = 0.089) or COVID-19 (6.9%; p = 0.037). Across pathogens, younger adults had relatively more comorbidities after adjusting for differences in the general population. They had shorter hospital stays and lower mortality, but higher intensive care unit admission rates. CONCLUSION Patients with RSV infection had a disease course comparable to patients with influenza or COVID-19 and a higher mortality rate, especially with increasing age. These findings highlight the importance of RSV vaccination in older adults and those with comorbidities, alongside established vaccination strategies for seasonal influenza and COVID-19.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to compare the risk profiles and outcomes of RSV, influenza, and COVID-19 infections in adults hospitalised in Belgium during the winter seasons of 2023/24 and 2024/25. It included 2,806 patients, with 535 having RSV infection, 1,694 influenza, and 577 COVID-19. The study found that patients with RSV were significantly older and had more comorbidities than those with influenza or COVID-19. RSV infection was associated with higher in-hospital mortality compared to both influenza and COVID-19. The results suggest that RSV vaccination should be prioritised for older adults and those with comorbidities, similar to current strategies for influenza and COVID-19. The study used multivariate analyses to compare age-related differences, but it does not report specific limitations or evidence strength assessment.

papers.title_zh: Characteristics and outcomes of adult patients hospitalised with RSV infection, influenza or COVID-19 in Belgium, winter seasons 2023/24 and 2024/25
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND Severe acute respiratory infections (SARI) cause substantial disease burden in older adults and those with comorbidities. AIM To inform Belgian vaccination policies, we aimed to compare risk profiles and outcomes of influenza, COVID-19 and RSV infections and examine age-related differences. METHODS Adults (≥ 18 years) hospitalised with SARI in nine Belgian sentinel hospitals during the 2023/24 and 2024/25 winter seasons were included. Patients with laboratory-confirmed RSV infection, influenza or COVID-19 were compared in terms of demographics, comorbidities, complications and outcomes. Adults 18–64 years were compared with those ≥ 65 years. Multivariate analyses were applied. RESULTS Among 2,806 patients, 535 (19.1%) had RSV infection, 1,694 (60.4%) influenza and 577 (20.6%) COVID-19. Patients with influenza were significantly younger (mean age 68.9 years) and had significantly fewer comorbidities (89.7%) than patients with RSV (73.8 years; 95.8%) or COVID-19 (74.0 years; 93.6%). Patients with COVID-19 experienced significantly fewer complications (40.8%) than patients with RSV (48.9%) or influenza (45.2%). Patients with RSV had higher in-hospital mortality (11.9%) than patients with influenza (7.3%; p = 0.089) or COVID-19 (6.9%; p = 0.037). Across pathogens, younger adults had relatively more comorbidities after adjusting for differences in the general population. They had shorter hospital stays and lower mortality, but higher intensive care unit admission rates. CONCLUSION Patients with RSV infection had a disease course comparable to patients with influenza or COVID-19 and a higher mortality rate, especially with increasing age. These findings highlight the importance of RSV vaccination in older adults and those with comorbidities, alongside established vaccination strategies for seasonal influenza and COVID-19.

papers.title: Development and application of nbLIBRA-seq for high-throughput discovery of antigen-specific nanobodies.
papers.abstract: Nanobodies are of high interest in many fields of medicine and biotechnology, although nanobody discovery has been limited by laborious screening techniques. Here, we demonstrate the successful adaptation of linking B cell receptor to antigen specificity through sequencing (LIBRA-seq) to immunized alpacas for the rapid identification of antigen-specific nanobodies, derived from heavy-chain antibodies. We validated LIBRA-seq for nanobody discovery (nbLIBRA-seq) in two different disease settings. First, we identified over 300 antigen-specific heavy-chain antibodies against human transferrin receptor (TfR1) from a single alpaca blood sample. Second, we tested the efficiency of nbLIBRA-seq with multiple antigens in the screening library. Using fusion glycoproteins from the related respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV), 1,125 antigen-specific heavy-chain-expressing B cells were recovered. Our results illustrate the potential of nbLIBRA-seq to rapidly identify antigen-specific heavy-chain antibodies for a range of diverse targets, a capability that will be critical for the efficient development of nanobody-based therapeutics.

papers.full_text: Abstract Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV) are major causes of acute respiratory tract infections in young children and share many epidemiological and clinical characteristics. This study aimed to compare the clinical characteristics, outcomes, and healthcare costs associated with RSV and hMPV infections in children younger than five years of age. In this retrospective comparative cohort study, children aged 1–71 months with laboratory-confirmed RSV or hMPV infection identified by multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction were included. RSV cases identified between September 2022 and April 2023 and hMPV cases identified between September 2022 and December 2025 were included. Both outpatient and hospitalized patients evaluated at a tertiary pediatric hospital were enrolled. A total of 693 children were included, comprising 547 with RSV infection and 146 with hMPV infection. Children with hMPV infection were significantly older and more frequently had underlying comorbidities than those with RSV infection. Bronchiolitis, cough, nasal congestion, tachypnea, chest retractions, rhonchi, oxygen supplementation, inhaled therapies, corticosteroid use, and hospitalization were more common among children with RSV infection (all p < 0.05). In contrast, pneumonia was more frequently observed in the hMPV group (p = 0.015). Lengths of hospital and pediatric intensive care unit stay were comparable between the groups (all p > 0.05). Conclusion: Consistent with previous studies, RSV and hMPV differed in age distribution, clinical presentation, and healthcare utilization. These data provide additional evidence from a tertiary pediatric center in Türkiye and support the generalizability of these observations across different geographic settings. | What is Known: • RSV and hMPV are major causes of acute respiratory tract infections in young children, but direct comparisons between these viruses remain limited. | | What is New: • In this large pediatric cohort, RSV predominantly affected younger children and was associated with more bronchiolitis, hospitalization, and supportive treatment needs, whereas hMPV was more common in older children with comorbidities and was more frequently associated with pneumonia. | Data availability The data that support the findings of this study are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request. The data are not publicly available because they contain information that could compromise the privacy of research participants. analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to compare the clinical characteristics, outcomes, and healthcare costs associated with RSV and hMPV infections in children younger than five years of age.
analysis.study_design_and_population: In this retrospective comparative cohort study, children aged 1–71 months with laboratory-confirmed RSV or hMPV infection identified by multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction were included. RSV cases identified between September 2022 and April 2023 and hMPV cases identified between September 2022 and December 2025 were included. Both outpatient and hospitalized patients evaluated at a tertiary pediatric hospital were enrolled.
analysis.methods: The study used multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction to identify laboratory-confirmed RSV and hMPV infections in children aged 1–71 months. Data were collected from a tertiary pediatric hospital and analyzed for clinical characteristics, outcomes, and healthcare costs.
analysis.main_results: Bronchiolitis, cough, nasal congestion, tachypnea, chest retractions, rhonchi, oxygen supplementation, inhaled therapies, corticosteroid use, and hospitalization were more common among children with RSV infection (all p < 0.05).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: This large pediatric cohort showed that RSV predominantly affected younger children and was associated with more bronchiolitis, hospitalization, and supportive treatment needs, whereas hMPV was more common in older children with comorbidities and was more frequently associated with pneumonia.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform targeted surveillance and management strategies for RSV infections in younger children, particularly in settings where hospitalization and supportive care are required.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a single tertiary pediatric center in Türkiye, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and potential geographic bias.

analysis.summary_en: This study compares the clinical characteristics and outcomes of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human metapneumovirus (hMPV) infections in children under five years of age. It is a retrospective comparative cohort study conducted at a tertiary pediatric hospital in Türkiye, including cases from September 2022 to December 2025. The study found that RSV infections were more common in younger children and associated with more severe symptoms such as bronchiolitis, hospitalization, and the need for supportive treatments, while hMPV was more frequently linked to pneumonia in older children with comorbidities. The results suggest that RSV and hMPV have distinct clinical impacts in this age group, which could inform targeted surveillance and management strategies. However, the study's findings may be limited by its focus on a single geographic location, which could affect generalizability. The evidence is considered moderate due to the observational design and potential for geographic bias.

elements_en.methods: The study used multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction to identify laboratory-confirmed RSV and hMPV infections in children aged 1–71 months. Data were collected from a tertiary pediatric hospital and analyzed for clinical characteristics, outcomes, and healthcare costs.
elements_en.main_results: Bronchiolitis, cough, nasal congestion, tachypnea, chest retractions, rhonchi, oxygen supplementation, inhaled therapies, corticosteroid use, and hospitalization were more common among children with RSV infection (all p < 0.05).
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: This large pediatric cohort showed that RSV predominantly affected younger children and was associated with more bronchiolitis, hospitalization, and supportive treatment needs, whereas hMPV was more common in older children with comorbidities and was more frequently associated with pneumonia.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform targeted surveillance and management strategies for RSV infections in younger children, particularly in settings where hospitalization and supportive care are required.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to a single tertiary pediatric center in Türkiye, which may affect the generalizability of the results. The evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and potential geographic bias.

papers.title: Human metapneumovirus in central China, 2024–2025: epidemiology, co-infections, and temporal dynamics
papers.abstract: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a major cause of acute respiratory infections in children, but comprehensive data from sentinel surveillance in the post‐pandemic period remain limited. Understanding its epidemiology and co‐infection patterns is critical for surveillance and prevention. We analyzed 36,143 respiratory specimens from ILI/SARI patients in Henan, China (2024–2025) using multiplex PCR for HMPV and 14 other pathogens. Positivity rates, enrichment ratios, co‐infection patterns, pathogen associations (OR/PR), and temporal dynamics (cross‐correlation and regression) were assessed. Overall HMPV positivity was 3.96% (1,432/36,143), with a sharp inter-year difference: 7.1% in 2024 vs. 1.7% in 2025, peaking at 26.2% during week 48. Children aged 3–5 years had the highest positivity (8.6%; enrichment ratio 2.18). Co-infections occurred in 56.2% of HMPV-positive cases, predominantly with Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae. HMPV showed positive associations with these bacteria (OR = 2.01 and 1.47, respectively) but negative associations with influenza virus (OR = 0.20) and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) (OR = 0.17). HBoV also showed a positive association (OR = 1.66). RSV positivity at a 1-week lag had a positive effect on HMPV (β = 0.15, P = 0.048). HMPV was frequently detected in pediatric ILI/SARI patients during 2024–2025, with high rates of bacterial co‐detection. The temporal lead‐lag relationship with RSV underscores the need for integrated surveillance and age‐targeted prevention. The marked 2024 resurgence warrants continued monitoring to determine whether the observed patterns represent a short‐term anomaly or a sustained change in HMPV circulation.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the epidemiology of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) in Henan, China, during 2024–2025, focusing on its co-infection patterns and temporal dynamics. The research aimed to fill knowledge gaps regarding HMPV's role in respiratory infections post-pandemic. Using multiplex PCR, the study analyzed 36,143 respiratory specimens from ILI/SARI patients, revealing an overall positivity rate of 3.96% with a notable inter-year variation. Children aged 3–5 years showed the highest HMPV positivity, and co-infections were common, particularly with Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae. HMPV was positively associated with HBoV and RSV at a 1-week lag, but negatively associated with influenza virus and RSV. These findings emphasize the need for integrated surveillance and age-specific prevention strategies, though the study's geographic limitation and reliance on sentinel data suggest moderate evidence strength.

papers.abstract_zh: 人偏肺病毒(HMPV)是儿童急性呼吸道感染的主要原因之一,但疫情后哨点监测的综合数据仍较为有限。了解其流行病学及共感染模式对于监测和预防至关重要。我们对2024–2025年中国河南省ILI/SARI患者的36,143份呼吸道样本进行了多重PCR检测,以识别HMPV及其他14种病原体。评估了阳性率、富集比、共感染模式、病原体关联性(OR/PR)以及时间动态(交叉相关性和回归分析)。总体HMPV阳性率为3.96%(1,432/36,143),且年际差异显著:2024年为7.1%,2025年为1.7%,在第48周达到峰值26.2%。3–5岁儿童的阳性率最高(8.6%;富集比2.18)。HMPV阳性病例中56.2%发生了共感染,主要与肺炎链球菌和流感嗜血杆菌相关。HMPV与这些细菌呈正相关(OR分别为2.01和1.47),但与流感病毒(OR = 0.20)和呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV,OR = 0.17)呈负相关。HMPV还与人类博卡病毒(HBoV)呈正相关(OR = 1.66)。RSV在1周滞后时的阳性率对HMPV有正向影响(β = 0.15,P = 0.048)。2024–2025年期间,HMPV在儿科ILI/SARI患者中频繁检出,且细菌共感染率较高。与RSV的时间领先滞后关系表明需要整合监测并针对年龄制定预防策略。2024年的显著回升提示应持续监测,以确定所观察到的模式是短期异常还是HMPV传播的持续变化。

papers.full_text: ABSTRACTBackground: Respiratory syncytial virus, a major cause of respiratory infections and hospitalizations in young children, especially bronchiolitis, is an important burden to the health system in Brazil. This study evaluated the trends, seasonality, and economic impact of hospitalizations associated with respiratory syncytial virus in Brazilian children.Methods: This study analyzed hospitalizations for acute bronchitis and bronchiolitis (International Code of Diseases-10 J20-J21) in Brazilian children <5 years of age from January 2014 and March 2025 using data from the Brazil’s Unified Health System. Annual trends were assessed with linear regression, while time series decomposition evaluated seasonality. Direct medical costs were adjusted for inflation and converted to international dollars (Int$). Pearson’s correlation coefficient was employed to analyze associations between length of stay and hospitalization cost. Results: A total of 727,808 hospitalizations were recorded, with 86.8% occurring in children under 5 years old. Hospitalizations increased by 307.8%, with marked declines in 2020 during the coronavirus disease-2019 pandemic and consistent seasonal peaks between March-June. Direct medical costs totaled Int$ 166.8 million, with 55.5% of expenditures after 2020. The mean cost per hospitalization increased by Int$ 21.48 between 2014-2024 (Int$ 118.16-139.64). Length of stay correlated moderately with cost (r = 0.55), particularly strongly in southeastern and southern Brazil. Conclusions: Our findings revealed distinct seasonal and regional patterns in hospitalizations and a post-pandemic increase in costs. The association between prolonged hospitalization and higher expenditures underscores the need for targeted, region-specific preventive strategies and timely clinical interventions, to reduce the growing economic burden on the system. METHODSStudy designThis study analyzed the trend in hospitalizations caused by RSV from 2014 to 2025 8 , estimating the direct medical costs based on monthly data grouped by Brazil’s geographical regions.The Brazilian macro-region (North, Northeast, Midwest, Southeast, and South) was used as the stratification variable, with data aggregated at the regional level by month of hospital admission and patient's region of residence.Data curationData were extracted on May 11 from the BUHS’s Hospital Information System (SIH) via the DATASUS TabNet tool using the filters “hospital morbidity” and “place of residence”, covering the timespan of January 2014 to March 2025 by region and federative unit 9 . The analysis included hospitalizations of children under 5 years of age (0-4 years), considering all admission types (elective or urgent) and care regime (public or private contracted to the BUHS). Hospitalizations financed exclusively by private health insurance or out-of-pocket payment are not recorded in SIH and are therefore not captured in this analysis. International Code of Diseases (ICD)-10 codes J20-J21 (bronchitis and bronchiolitis) were selected 10 . Case definition was based solely on ICD-10 administrative coding, without laboratory confirmation; therefore, RSV cannot be directly attributed to individual hospitalizations, and the term 'potentially associated with RSV' is used throughout to reflect this limitation. Data were exported as .csv files and processed using R Foundation for Statistical Computing, Viena, Áustria, for organization, cleaning, and aggregation to support the statistical and temporal analyses 9 , 10 . Data extracted for the period January-March 2025 were considered preliminary, as records from the last 6 months in SIH/DATASUS are subject to consolidation updates; these data though included in descriptive and cost analyses, should be cautiously interpreted.Time series analysis: hospitalization’s annual growth rateThe annual growth rate was estimated using a simple linear regression model (Equation 1): Y=β0+ β1X+ε (1) where Y is the number of monthly hospitalizations, X is time (in months), is the intercept, β1 is the mean monthly increase or decrease rate (annualized estimates in the Results were calculated as 12×β1), and ε is the error term.The analyses were conducted using the R software 11 , using the core packages (I) ggplot2 12 for graphical display, (II) dplyr 13 for data manipulation, (III) readxl 14 for reading Excel files, (IV) patchwork 15 for combining graphics, combination, and (V) lubridate 16 for date manipulation. The trend line from linear regression was automatically adjusted with the geom_smooth (method = “lm”) function in ggplot2 12 , which estimated the coefficients (β0 and β1) and illustrated the fitted line.Time series decompositionFollowing linear analysis, time series decomposition was performed 17 , 18 . Data were aggregated by month for each region and converted into time series objects (ts) in R software via the stats package 11 . Each series was assigned a monthly frequency (12 per year), spanning January 2014 to December 2024 (complete annual cycles; the three months of partial 2025 data were excluded from the decomposition to avoid distortion of the seasonal component, while descriptive and cost analyses include data through March 2025). The decomposition differentiated the trend, seasonal, and residual components. Seasonal factors were examined to characterize and validate temporal patterns. Decomposition was performed with the decompose function (stats package) 11 for each regional and national time series. Graphs were generated using the ggplot2 14 autoplot function and organized to emphasize regional disparities.Autocorrelation analysis 19 , 20 was employed to detect temporal dependencies and seasonality in Brazil and its regions, using the acf function from the stats package 11 . It measured correlations at different lags and graphs were generated through the ggAcf function (forecast package) 21 , to identify short-term dependencies and seasonal or cyclical patterns across time scales.Direct medical cost estimationDirect medical costs of hospitalizations caused by RSV were estimated for 2014-2025. Mean costs per hospitalization were calculated annually for Brazil and each of its five regions. Boxplots were generated using ggplot2 (geom_boxplot) 12 to illustrate the annual dispersion of mean hospitalization costs. Descriptive statistics, including standard deviation and variance of mean values, were calculated for each year and region using dplyr functions 13 .The correlation between mean length of stay and mean direct medical cost per hospitalization was estimated using the cor function (stats package) 11 . A simple linear regression model (lm function) was applied to assess the association between average length of stay (independent variable) and adjusted average cost per hospitalization (dependent variable), corrected for inflation and converted to international dollars (Int$) using the purchasing power parity (PPP) conversion factor of 2.524 BRL/Int$, as recommended by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development and the World Bank 22 , 23 . Pearson’s correlation coefficient was employed to measure the strength and direction of the linear relationship between mean length of stay and mean direct medical cost per hospital stay 24 , 25 . Scatter plots were generated for each region, with trend lines based on the fitted regression model using geom_point function to plot the scatter points and geom_smooth (method = “lm”) from ggplot2 14 to add the regression line. Correlation strength was interpreted according to conventional thresholds.Inflation adjustment and currency conversionTo ensure temporal comparability, hospitalization costs were adjusted for inflation using Brazil’s extended national consumer price index provided by the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (SIDRA table 1737, national level) 26 . Monthly values were aggregated by calendar year, and the national average for 2024 was adopted as the reference base year.For international comparability, inflation-adjusted values were converted to Int$ using Brazil’s 2024 PPP conversion factor of 2.524 BRL/Int$, as published by the World Bank 23 . A fixed PPP factor was utilized to present the historical series in standardized purchasing power, reflecting the actual economic burden of hospitalization costs in Brazil. All PPP conversions were applied exclusively to inflation-adjusted BRL values, following international best practices 22 . Ethical considerationsThis study was approved by the research ethics committee of the Gonçalo Moniz Research Center (approval no. 6.929.375 and IORG0002090/OMB no. 0990-0279) and complied with the Brazilian National Health Council Resolution CNS no. 466/2012. The databases included anonymized information from the Hospital Information System and the Mortality Information System, accessed via TABWIN and TABNET platforms (DATASUS) under e-SIC protocols no. 25072.028465/2024-98 and no. 25072.017378/2024-13. Study designThis study analyzed the trend in hospitalizations caused by RSV from 2014 to 2025 8 , estimating the direct medical costs based on monthly data grouped by Brazil’s geographical regions.The Brazilian macro-region (North, Northeast, Midwest, Southeast, and South) was used as the stratification variable, with data aggregated at the regional level by month of hospital admission and patient's region of residence. RESULTSBetween January 2014 and March 2025, Brazil reported 727,808 hospitalizations for acute bronchitis and acute bronchiolitis; of these, 86.8% (n = 631,724/727,808) occurred in children < 5 years of age. From 2014 to 2024, total hospitalizations increased by 307.8% (Figure 1). The southeastern region showed the highest increase (135.9%), followed by the northeastern (67.9%), midwestern (48.9%), and southern (48.5%) regions; northern Brazil had the lowest increase (6.6%). There was a marked national decline in 2020, corresponding to the first year of the coronavirus disease-2019 (COVID-19) pandemic (Figure 1). FIGURE 1:Trend in hospitalizations for bronchitis and acute bronchiolitis by month and year of care (2014-2025). Source: Brazilian Ministry of Health 12 . Data for the last 6 months, subject to change. Overall, hospitalizations rose significantly (128,6%) from 3548 in July 2014 to 8110 in June 2023. Residuals reflected variations such as the abrupt decline at the start of the COVID-19 pandemic (-3293 in April 2020) and isolated spikes (1742 in June 2023), a trend present in all regions. Seasonality remained stable, with a consistent annual cycle across regions (Supplementary Figure 1). In the midwest region, hospitalizations increased by 207% (from 265 in July 2014 to 814 in September 2024), with a decrease of 489 cases in April 2020, potentially attributed to the pandemic. In the northeast, the trend rose 143% (from 715 to 1740), also with notable residuals in 2020. The north experienced a more modest growth (54%; from 331 to 511), with reductions in May 2020 (- 353) and increases in May 2023 (+ 383). In the southeast, hospitalizations increased 108% (from 1538 in July 2014 to 3205 in September 2024), with residuals reducing in April 2020 (- 2113) and growing in March 2023 (+ 1266). In the south, cases grew from 700 in January 2014 to 1290 in September 2024, with residuals declining in June 2020 (- 840) during the pandemic (Supplementary Figure 1). Autocorrelation analysis indicated a seasonality at lag 12 (ACF = 0.60) in Brazil. The southeast (0.60) and south (0.64) had the strongest annual seasonality, followed by the midwest (0.57) and northeast (0.59). The north showed a weaker pattern (0.52) (Supplementary Figure 2).Regional boxplots exhibited a consistent seasonality, with hospitalization peaks between March and June. April and May had the highest median values in most regions. Nationally, the peak occurred between March and July, suggesting a consolidated epidemic pattern. In the northeast, north, and midwest, hospitalizations increased from March to June. In the south and southeast, seasonality persisted longer, with elevated rates until mid-August. From August to December, all regions showed lower medians and interquartile ranges, expressing reduced hospitalization rates (Figure 2). FIGURE 2:Hospitalizations for bronchitis and acute bronchiolitis potentially associated with respiratory syncytial virus cases by month and year (2014-2025). Source: Brazilian Ministry of Health 12 . Data for the last 6 months, subject to change. Between 2014-2025, hospitalizations for acute bronchitis and bronchiolitis in children aged <5 years resulted in Int$ 166.8 million. From 2020 to 2024, Int$ 92.5 million was spent (approximately 55.48% of the total), a 29.1% increase compared to that in the pre-pandemic period (2014-2019), when expenditures totaled Int$ 71.7 million, underscoring the substantial economic impact of the post-COVID-19 period on pediatric respiratory hospitalizations (Table 1).
